Rules / Maintainability

SK7070 An obsolete marker has no message

Obsolete is applied with no message, or with a placeholder message, so no caller is told what to use instead.

CategoryMaintainability
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3
SupersedesS1123

Why

An obsolescence is a migration instruction addressed to every caller. Without a message the compiler warning says only that something is deprecated, and the reader has to find the replacement by archaeology. This is the same requirement SK7050 and SK7051 make of a suppression, on the other side of the conversation: the annotation that changes what other code should do carries the reason. The tool reports the omission and never invents the replacement, because a manufactured message would be worse than none.

Example

Instead of:

[Obsolete]
public void Save() { }

Write:

[Obsolete("Use SaveAsync; this overload blocks the calling thread.")]
public void Save() { }

When it does not fire

Only attributes that semantically resolve to System.ObsoleteAttribute are inspected, so a user attribute with the same short name is ignored. The message argument is resolved against the constructor's parameter list, so the positional and message: spellings are one answer. A non-constant expression is accepted without inspection rather than guessed at. Empty, whitespace and TODO/FIXME/TBD/N/A placeholders are not treated as messages; the rule cannot assess whether otherwise substantive prose actually names a replacement. DiagnosticId and UrlFormat are not accepted as substitutes, because neither is shown in the compiler's warning text.

Configuration

  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK7070.severity
